correctness.rationale: The coordinate change is an invertible projective transformation and exact substitution identifies the two quartic equations. Exact symbolic replay maps the eight listed inner Galois points to the two four-point coordinate-line sets, verifies all 16 joins lie on the Schur quartic and are pairwise distinct, and verifies K4,4 incidence. Rojas--Lira Lemma 3.1 proves these 16 are all Schur lines meeting either coordinate line, so each transformed Galois point has exactly four incident Schur lines. Nurowski gives a complete census with exactly eight quadruple points and characterizes the corresponding 16-line skeleton, completing the exhaustion argument. The finite computation is not used as a substitute for the published global 64-line census.

value.rationale: The maximal number of inner Galois points and the maximal 64-line quartic are two natural extremal structures on smooth quartic K3 surfaces. Identifying them on the same surface and showing that the Galois points are precisely the intrinsic quadruple points of the line configuration gives a canonical incidence-theoretic interpretation of all eight Galois points. The K4,4 structure is not an arbitrary slice: it is the entire 16-line skeleton singled out intrinsically by line multiplicity, while the remaining 48 lines avoid every Galois point.
